items.title: Rookie Councillor's Six-Month Climb From Fourth Place Ends in Mississauga's Top Job
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Alvin Tedjo, a first-term city councillor, has won Mississauga's mayoral race after his campaign started in a distant fourth place six months ago. According to the newspaper, the 43-year-old overtook incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor, former mayor and Ontario Liberal leader Bonnie Crombie, who had held a narrow lead in polling heading into election day. The Star reports that with 89 per cent of polls reporting on election night, Tedjo led by more than 18,000 votes. At his victory party, Tedjo told cheering supporters that Mississauga had voted for change, and said that when his team started out, people had told them they could not win. According to the outlet, Crombie called Tedjo to congratulate him and, standing on stage with her three children, said his energy and enthusiasm had inspired people to believe they could help shape the city's future.

items.title: Brampton Man Surrenders Hours After Police Release His Description in Fatal Mississauga Stabbing
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a Brampton man has been charged with second-degree murder in connection with a deadly stabbing in Mississauga over the weekend. According to Peel Regional Police, the suspect they had been searching for since the stabbing was reported early Sunday morning turned himself in to homicide detectives on Monday afternoon. The outlet reports police had issued a release earlier that day identifying him and urging him to seek legal counsel and surrender. According to the outlet, the stabbing happened in a parking lot in an industrial area near Tomken Road and Kamato Road in Mississauga's east end, where officers found a man with life-threatening injuries who was pronounced dead at the scene despite first responders' efforts. The outlet reports police had earlier described the suspect as a Black man with a large build, long dreadlocked hair and a tattoo of five stars on his left upper cheek. According to insauga.com, Kevin Chippie, 35, of Brampton, turned himself in and was charged with second-degree murder, and the investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: Urban Capital Takes Over Final Three Towers of Mississauga's M City Megaproject
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the remaining development lands at Mississauga's M City condo community have changed hands. According to the outlet, Urban Capital has acquired the land for the project's final three towers, M6, M7 and M8, from Rogers Real Estate Development Limited. The outlet reports M City launched in 2017 at Burnhamthorpe Road West and Confederation Parkway, with five of its eight planned towers, M1 through M5, now completed or under construction, including the 83-storey M3, which Urban Capital says will be the tallest skyscraper in Mississauga. According to insauga.com, the full 15-acre community is planned to eventually include more than 6,000 homes, retail and office space, and over two acres of new public parkland. Mark Reeve, a partner at Urban Capital, told the outlet the company has been involved with M City since the beginning and has a deep connection to the community and its future.

items.title: University of Toronto Professor Calls Mississauga's Mayoral Race Unusually Rare Matchup
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga's 2026 mayoral race has turned into an unusually tight contest as voters head to the polls. According to the outlet, the campaign began with two clear front-runners, incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie, who left the mayor's chair early in 2024 after a decade in office to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. The outlet reports city councillors Alvin Tedjo of Ward 2 and Dipika Damerla of Ward 7 also entered the race with recognizable names, though neither was initially expected to mount a serious challenge. According to insauga.com, recent polling suggests Tedjo has gained enough ground to turn the contest into a genuine three-way race heading into election day. Randy Besco, an associate professor of political science at the University of Toronto Mississauga, told the outlet it is unusual in municipal politics for a sitting mayor to face a serious challenge from her own predecessor, describing it as effectively having two incumbents competing for the same job.
